newsitem.title: UK: SFA fines UBS, disciplines traders for breaches.
newsitem.headline: SFA fines UBS, disciplines traders for breaches.

text.p: The UK's Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Tuesday it had fined UBS Ltd 20,000 stg and required the investment bank to pay costs of 8,000 stg "for matters relating to mismarking of positions".

The watchdog said in a statement it had also disciplined former UBS warrants and convertibles traders James Keen and Mark Larkin following the conclusion of proceedings it instituted in June and July 1995.
UBS Ltd is part of Union Bank of Switzerland.

Larkin, who was head of convertibles and warrants trading at UBS, has been expelled from the SFA's register of managers, fined 10,000 stg and required to pay costs of 4,500 stg while Keen has been reprimanded, fined 2,000 stg and required to pay costs of 6,000 stg, the SFA said.
UBS and Larkin settled separately with the SFA while Keen took his case to the watchdog's disciplinary tribunal.

The SFA said UBS had admitted it had failed "between March and May 1994 to speedily identify and remedy the fact that a number of positions held by the convertibles and warrants desk had been mismarked".
The SFA said this breached its rules on marking to market, adding that UBS had "failed to conduct its fortnightly mark reviews in a proper and effective manner".

When the positions were revalued in accordance with SFA's rules, there was a divergence of 8.9 million stg between the level at which the positions had been marked and their market value, the SFA said.

The watchdog said it had taken into account the prompt reporting of the mismarking, the complete cooperation of UBS with the SFA, and that "at the material time, adequate external price fixes were not available".

In addition UBS had, by mid-1994, strengthened its review process on its own initiative. The fact that the divergence values "were not material in context, carried no significant business risk and did not breach UBS' capital adequacy requirements", had also been taken into account, the SFA said.
It said Larkin had admitted he had ultimate responsibility for ensuring the accuracy of the marks and that he failed to ensure the positions in question were marked in accordance with SFA's rules.
He had also disobeyed an instruction, between July and October 1994, not to increase positions.
"He concealed the trades he undertook in breach of that instruction by failing to book them on execution and by warehousing (them) with his French counterparty," it added.

The SFA said it had taken into account Larkin's full cooperation during the course of the investigations. It said he was not currently registered with it and details of the action against him had been routinely notified to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
Keen was found by the SFA's disciplinary tribunal to have applied an inappropriate marking policy in his marking of five positions and by omitting to mark three positions to market.

The SFA accepted Keen's marking policy was a house policy that he was authorised to apply. This involved marking long positions at a premium over bid "to reflect short hedge positions which were also held by the desk on the basis that the positions were held as swap positions".
But there was no active swap market in the securities at the time in question and the positions were not marked at their market value in accordance with SFA's rules.
The SFA confirmed that, except for the matters which were the subject of the charge, its investigations into Keen's activities while employed at UBS "disclosed no other matters of concern".
"In fixing the penalty the tribunal had regard to Keen's seniority on the desk and the value placed on his performance by UBS," the SFA said, adding that Keen was not registered with it.
-- Alexander Smith, London Newsroom ++ 44 171 542 7719
